clue.text: Bleat about bread being a 9

indicators.note: about means the sheep's cry is wrapped round the next piece

parts.note: a sheep's bleat is its baa
naan (or nan) is Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: Someone bleats on about bread, which turns out to be a ready-made snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a 9' points to 9 across, a convenience food; a banana needs no cooking at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is the ultimate ready-to-eat snack, nature's own packaged food needing no preparation.

clue.text: Lifting a jumper in error is rude

indicators.note: in puts the turned animal inside the mistake

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a roo, or kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: Taking someone's sweater by mistake is bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' reads as the British word for a sweater but means a kangaroo. 'Lifting' reads upwards in a down clue, so the animal is turned backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish means rude and ill-mannered, behaving like a lout.

clue.text: What's contemplated is a bit flipping irrelevant

indicators.note: flipping signals a turn so the extracted letters run backwards
a bit means just a portion of the word is taken

explanation.surface: What's being pondered is a bit flipping irrelevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swearword but reverses LEVAN, taken from inside 'irrelevant'. Navel-gazing is self-absorbed contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemplating one's navel is the idiom for self-absorbed meditation.

clue.text: Girl following nose, we hear

parts.note: nose said out loud is noes, and the girl who comes after two noes is the heroine of the musical No, No

explanation.walkthrough: 'nose' sounds like 'noes'; the musical's title follows 'No, No' with the girl's name. It gave us the song 'Tea for Two'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nanette is a girl's name and the title character of the 1925 musical comedy.

clue.text: Curve at point on River Spree

parts.note: a curve is a bend
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A bend at some spot on the River Spree in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spree is a Berlin river, but here 'Spree' is the definition: a drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is British slang for a drinking binge, a spree of heavy boozing.

clue.text: Goes further than former favourites at 24, say

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: former is ex, and favourites at Flushing Meadows are the seeded tennis players, seeds

explanation.surface: Past favourites at a tennis venue go further than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is Flushing Meadows, the US Open tennis venue, where favourites are seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed is to go beyond or surpass, going further than a limit.

clue.text: One producingdischarge from army, initially, in case of deserter

indicators.note: in case of means placed inside the outer casing of the next word

parts.note: a deserter is a defector, one who abandons their side

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of army

explanation.surface: A soldier discharged from the army after deserting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' suggests release from military service, but the definition is crude: someone discharging waste.
explanation.definitionFit: A defecator is one who empties the bowels, producing a bodily discharge.

clue.text: Bird set off in company of men going both ways

indicators.note: in company of means sitting among, so it goes inside
going both ways means the soldiers appear once backwards and once forwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: off signals the letters are set off, moved out of order

explanation.surface: A bird sets off among a group of men heading in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'men', supplies the soldiers twice, once in each direction, and the rearranged 'set' sits between the two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic fowl, a cockerel.

clue.text: Sheep's upset about ram's initial complaint

indicators.note: about here means the jumbled flock goes round the letter
upset says the letters are knocked over and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of ram

explanation.surface: Sheep are distressed about a ram's first illness.
explanation.walkthrough: SHEEP rearranged gives HEPES, and 'about' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Herpes is a viral infection, a complaint in the sense of a medical ailment.

clue.text: WC Fields starting to overdose when eating duck as ready meal?

parts.note: a WC, or public lavatory, is euphemistically a convenience

indicators.note: starting asks for the opening letter of the word Fields
eating means one piece swallows another inside it

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: The comedian W.C. Fields begins overdosing while eating duck, presented as a ready meal.
explanation.walkthrough: W.C. Fields was an American comic actor; here the WC is split off as a lavatory. A convenience is the British euphemism for a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Convenience food is a prepared meal needing little cooking, such as a microwave dinner.

clue.text: Girl having to live rough

indicators.note: rough suggests something done roughly or crudely, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A young woman forced to sleep rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet is a girl's given name, taken from the flower.

clue.text: MP with somewhere to sleep in the city when not working

indicators.note: in places the bed inside what remains of the city
not says the letters for working are dropped

parts.note: Preston is a city in Lancashire
on means working, as a machine that is on
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A politician who keeps a bed in town for when Parliament is not sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link, and 'not working' strips the word for working from the city. John Prescott was a Labour MP and Deputy Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: John Prescott was a long-serving Labour Member of Parliament for Hull and Deputy Prime Minister.

clue.text: Book referred to with honour in dailies

indicators.note: in puts the award inside the cleaners

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning lady
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A book mentioned alongside an honours list in the daily papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dailies' looks like newspapers but means chars, cleaning women who come in daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers is a well-known British dictionary, a reference book that people consult.

clue.text: Show-off's first statement of intent

parts.note: to show is to manifest

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of off

explanation.surface: A show-off's opening declaration of what they mean to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published declaration of a party's aims and policies.

clue.text: Give it a go for God!

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
a go is a turn, as in taking turns

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to have a try: give it a go, for God's sake!
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention from the old slang 'she's got it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the Roman god of agriculture and time, father of Jupiter.

clue.text: Drunk like some 9s

definitions.meaning: slang for drunk, tinned or tanked up
many convenience foods come preserved in tins

explanation.definitionFit: Canned is slang for intoxicated, and also describes food sold preserved in a tin.

clue.text: Fibre replacing Lycra in crop tops

indicators.note: replacing read as re-placing, putting the letters in again in a new order
tops asks for the first letter of each word in and crop

explanation.surface: A man-made fibre stands in for Lycra in cropped tops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crop tops' looks like short garments; 'tops' takes the first letters of 'in crop', giving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre used in knitwear and fabrics.

clue.text: Prevent from having letter about 25 cropped

indicators.note: about means the spelt-out letter goes round the shortened word

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D

indicators.note: cropped means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: 25 is closet, and an old word for a closet or toilet is privy

explanation.surface: To stop someone having a letter about a cropped item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropped' cuts the last letter from PRIVY, giving PRIV.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprive someone is to deny them or stop them having something.

clue.text: The whole thing's about serving men

indicators.note: about here means the word for thing goes round the soldiers

parts.note: a thing is an entity
the RE, the Royal Engineers, are serving soldiers

explanation.surface: Everything someone owns concerns the men serving them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thing's' reads as thing has, with 'about' saying ENTITY surrounds RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirety means the whole of something, all of it taken together.

clue.text: One of the 26 sat in MG, shortly to come out

indicators.note: sat in means placed inside the car's letters
shortly says the spelt-out letters are cut short by one

parts.note: MG spelt out is em-gee, the British sports car marque
26 is queens, and ER (Elizabeth Regina) is one queen

explanation.surface: A queen sits in an MG sports car, about to emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: MG is a classic British sports car; 'shortly' trims the spelt-out letters of its name by one E before the queen is seated inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view.

clue.text: Original "back to nature" author?

indicators.note: original here means made new, so the letters are recast
back to picks the last letter of nature

explanation.surface: The writer who first championed returning to the simple natural life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to nature' gives E, its last letter, which joins the letters of 'author' for the rearrangement. Thoreau wrote Walden about living in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, author of Walden, was an early advocate of simple living in nature.

clue.text: Hols ruined with wet Wednesday in Yorkshire

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Holidays spoilt by a rainy Wednesday in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield Wednesday is a Yorkshire football club nicknamed The Owls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Owls is the nickname of Sheffield Wednesday Football Club.

clue.text: Charts prove an asset, it's said, for an oldbattleship

indicators.note: it's said tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: charts are graphs, and to prove an asset is to pay

explanation.surface: Charts turn out to be useful for a historic warship.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEE is pronounced 'spay', so GRAPHS PAY gives the ship's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Admiral Graf Spee was a German pocket battleship scuttled off Montevideo in 1939.

clue.text: Clobber soiled for those of a certain age

indicators.note: to clobber something is to batter it, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Dirty clothes for older people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' reads as a noun for clothing, but it is the verb, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldies is an affectionate word for older people, folk of a certain age.

clue.text: US car's shortened bumper

indicators.note: shortened means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a dodgem is a fairground bumper car

explanation.surface: An American car's bumper has been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumper' looks like part of the car but is a dodgem, the fairground bumper car.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodge is an American car brand made by Chrysler.

clue.text: Like a WC Fields set location?

parts.note: a WC is flushing when its cistern empties
fields are meadows

explanation.surface: A setting described like the comedian W.C. Fields.
explanation.walkthrough: A tennis set is played at Flushing Meadows, home of the US Open in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Flushing Meadows, in the borough of Queens, New York, hosts the US Open tennis championship.

clue.text: Near defeat, finally, at 24 location? We're not out yet

parts.note: near means close

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word defeat

parts.note: Flushing Meadows lies in Queens, a borough of New York

explanation.surface: Close to losing at the end of a match at the US Open venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link. Closet queens are gay men who have not come out.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet queen is a gay man who has not publicly come out, so still hidden.

clue.text: See 25
